checker_results.pass_1_fix: One cause, two symptoms. The object file's provenance comment contained the literal string '--manifest-dir'; '--' is illegal inside an XML comment, so the file did not parse, so collect_assignments() indexed no override, so the page correctly reported as unassigned. Reworded to 'its manifest-dir argument'. No metadata element changed. The second ERROR is the checker's headline finding working exactly as designed - it is what separates a deployed page from a visible one - and it disappeared with the parse failure.
checker_results.reading: Exit 0 with zero warnings is the meaningful result here, not just a clean bill: the zero-warning half means no override in this tree points at a page outside it, and the no-ERROR half means the page IS pointed at. --strict was deliberately not passed, per the step's declared command; it would promote the outside-the-tree warning to an error, and there is nothing in this tree for it to catch. Empty-directory behaviour, per the step's test description: exit 1 on 'no flexipages/*.flexipage-meta.xml found'.
